title: Prisoners Assigned Burial Labor
summary: Lamanite prisoners were placed under guard and compelled to bury their dead and slain Nephites, with Moroni assigning men to guard them during their labors.
characters: Men placed as guards by Moroni

explicit_facts.text: Guards were set over the prisoners of the Lamanites.
The prisoners were compelled to go forth and bury their dead and the slain Nephites.
Moroni placed men over the prisoners to guard them during their labors.

unspecified_visual_details: The location, number of prisoners and guards, clothing, tools, and burial arrangements are unspecified.
Moroni's physical presence during the burial labor is unspecified.

narration.text: And it came to pass that they did set guards over the prisoners of the Lamanites, and did compel them to go forth and bury their dead, yea, and also the dead of the Nephites who were slain;

doctrinal_or_story_notes: Mormon is the narrator; no direct speech is supplied.
Retain this as a narrated report rather than staging a newly invented present-tense burial scene.
The verse does not establish a separate chronological sequence between setting guards and Moroni placing men over the prisoners.
prohibited_inventions: Do not stage the reported actions as a single specified moment or invent an order for the guard assignments.
Do not identify the unspecified 'they' or attribute the compulsion specifically to Moroni.
Do not add dialogue, named prisoners, individual identities for the dead, or motives.
Do not depict Moroni as necessarily present during the burial work.
Do not depict wounds, blood, or severed body parts.

title: Lehi Takes Command of Mulek
summary: Moroni and Lehi go to Mulek; Moroni gives Lehi command of the city.

explicit_facts.text: Moroni went to Mulek with Lehi, took command of the city, and gave it to Lehi.
Lehi had been with Moroni in most of his battles, and the two rejoiced in each other's safety and were beloved by each other and the people of Nephi.

reasonable_visual_inferences: Moroni and Lehi stand together in the city during the transfer of command.
unspecified_visual_details: Their clothing, ages, appearance, and the manner in which command was transferred.

narration.text: Moroni went to the city of Mulek with Lehi
and gave it unto Lehi

prohibited_inventions: Do not depict a specific ceremony or invent words spoken by either man.

title: Digging the Ditch at Bountiful
summary: After burying their dead and the Nephite dead, the Lamanites were marched back into Bountiful. By Moroni's orders, Teancum caused them to begin digging a ditch around the land or city of Bountiful.

explicit_facts.text: The Lamanites finished burying their dead and the dead of the Nephites before being marched back into Bountiful.
By Moroni's orders, Teancum caused the Lamanites to begin digging a ditch around the land or city of Bountiful.

reasonable_visual_inferences: Lamanites beginning ditch work at Bountiful.
unspecified_visual_details: The number of Lamanites, the tools used, and the ditch's exact shape and dimensions.
Whether Teancum is physically present at the digging.

narration.text: And it came to pass that after the Lamanites had finished burying their dead and also the dead of the Nephites, they were marched back into the land Bountiful; and Teancum, by the orders of Moroni, caused that they should commence laboring in digging a ditch round about the land, or the city, Bountiful.

doctrinal_or_story_notes: The burial and march precede the ditch work; they are not simultaneous actions in this scene.
prohibited_inventions: Do not depict the earlier burial or march as occurring during the ditch work.
Do not depict Moroni as physically present or invent dialogue, escorts, or burial details.

title: Building Bountiful's Wall
summary: Prisoners build a high encircling wall using timbers and earth from the ditch.

explicit_facts.text: They built a timber breastwork on the inner bank of the ditch and piled excavated dirt against it, encircling Bountiful with a high, strong wall of timber and earth.

reasonable_visual_inferences: Prisoners lift timbers and move earth as the defensive wall takes shape.
unspecified_visual_details: The wall's exact dimensions, construction tools, and individual workers' appearance.

narration.text: a strong wall of timbers and earth

prohibited_inventions: Do not add battle or depict the wall being attacked.

title: Prisoners Guarded Within the Wall
summary: The completed wall becomes a stronghold, and Lamanite prisoners are guarded within it.

explicit_facts.text: Bountiful became a stronghold; Lamanite prisoners were guarded inside the wall they had built.
Moroni had the prisoners labor because they were easy to guard while working, and he wanted all his forces available for a future attack.

reasonable_visual_inferences: The wall encloses the prisoners as guards watch over them.
unspecified_visual_details: The guards' number and arrangement, and whether prisoners are working at the depicted instant.

narration.text: they did guard the prisoners of the Lamanites

doctrinal_or_story_notes: Moroni's stated desire for his forces is an explanation, not a narrated attack.
prohibited_inventions: Do not show a new attack or battle.

title: Retrospective Account of Mulek
summary: Moroni had gained a victory over a Lamanite army, obtained possession of Mulek, and built a stronghold to retain his prisoners.

explicit_facts.text: Moroni had gained a victory over one of the greatest armies of the Lamanites.
Moroni had obtained possession of Mulek, one of the strongest Lamanite holds in the land of Nephi.
Moroni had built a stronghold to retain his prisoners.

unspecified_visual_details: The appearance of Mulek and the design and location of the stronghold are unspecified.

narration.text: Moroni had thus gained a victory over one of the greatest of the armies of the Lamanites,
and had obtained possession of the city of Mulek, which was one of the strongest holds of the Lamanites in the land of Nephi;
and thus he had also built a stronghold to retain his prisoners.

doctrinal_or_story_notes: The verse reports completed events retrospectively; it does not place them at one moment.
prohibited_inventions: Do not stage an ongoing battle, the taking of Mulek, and stronghold construction as simultaneous events.
Do not depict Moroni as physically present in a current scene or invent the appearance of the city, stronghold, or prisoners.

title: Preparing for War
summary: Moroni does not attempt another battle that year; his men prepare for war, fortify defenses, deliver women and children from famine and affliction, and provide food for the armies.

explicit_facts.text: Moroni made no further attempt to battle that year; his men prepared for war and made fortifications against the Lamanites.
They delivered their women and children from famine and affliction and provided food for their armies.

reasonable_visual_inferences: A single moment of fortification work may include supplies being carried nearby.
unspecified_visual_details: Which particular fortification or food distribution to depict, and the people's specific appearance.

narration.text: he did employ his men in preparing for war
providing food for their armies

prohibited_inventions: Do not depict an unreported battle or specific rescue.

title: Lamanites Gain Ground
summary: While Moroni is absent because of intrigue and dissensions among the Nephites, Lamanite armies by the west sea in the south gain ground over the Nephites and obtain possession of a number of their cities.
locations: Cities in that part of the land

explicit_facts.text: The armies of the Lamanites were on the west sea, south.
Moroni was absent on account of intrigue among the Nephites, which caused dissensions among them.
The Lamanite armies gained ground over the Nephites and obtained possession of a number of their cities in that part of the land.

reasonable_visual_inferences: Lamanite forces may be shown in a city they already possess, without depicting its capture.
unspecified_visual_details: The number of cities and the circumstances of their capture.

narration.text: the armies of the Lamanites, on the west sea, south, while in the absence of Moroni on account of some intrigue amongst the Nephites, which caused dissensions amongst them, had gained some ground over the Nephites, yea, insomuch that they had obtained possession of a number of their cities in that part of the land.

doctrinal_or_story_notes: Mormon reports territorial gains and possession of cities; the verse does not narrate a specific battle.
prohibited_inventions: Do not depict an unreported battle or the moment of capture.

title: Nephites in Danger
summary: The account attributes the Nephites' dangerous circumstances to iniquity, dissensions, and intrigue among themselves.

explicit_facts.text: Because of iniquity, dissensions, and intrigue among themselves, the Nephites were placed in dangerous circumstances.

reasonable_visual_inferences: Use off-screen narration over a neutral, supported setting rather than inventing a gathering or confrontation.

title: The People of Ammon Protected
summary: Mormon recounts that the people of Ammon, formerly Lamanites, were converted, brought to Zarahemla, and protected by the Nephites. Their oath kept them from taking up arms or shedding blood.

explicit_facts.text: The people of Ammon were formerly Lamanites and had been converted unto the Lord by Ammon and his brethren, or rather by the power and word of God.
They were brought to the land of Zarahemla and protected by the Nephites.
Their oath kept them from taking up arms against their brethren; they had sworn never to shed blood again.
Mormon says they would have suffered themselves to fall into their brethren's hands but for the pity and love of Ammon and his brethren.

reasonable_visual_inferences: The people of Ammon may be shown as a group in Zarahemla without staging a specific past event.
unspecified_visual_details: Their clothing, ages, and individual appearances are not specified.
The appearance of Zarahemla is not specified.

narration.text: I have somewhat to say concerning the people of Ammon
they had been brought down into the land of Zarahemla, and had ever since been protected by the Nephites.
they had taken an oath that they never would shed blood more

doctrinal_or_story_notes: Conversion, relocation, and protection are reported as earlier events, not actions occurring in this scene.
The account attributes their conversion ultimately to the power and word of God.
prohibited_inventions: Do not depict Ammon or his brethren as physically present.
Do not stage a conversion, oath-taking, attack, or rescue; none is narrated as occurring at this moment.
Do not invent dialogue or a particular act of Nephite protection.

title: Helaman Persuades the People of Ammon
summary: The people of Ammon see the Nephites' danger and afflictions and desire to defend their country. As they are about to take their weapons, Helaman and his brethren persuade them; taking up arms would break their oath. Helaman fears they might lose their souls, and those who made the covenant must behold their brethren endure afflictions.

explicit_facts.text: The people of Ammon are moved with compassion by the danger and afflictions the Nephites bear for them and desire to take up arms in defense of their country.
As they are about to take their weapons, the persuasions of Helaman and his brethren stop them from breaking their oath.
Helaman fears they might lose their souls; those who entered the covenant must behold their brethren in dangerous circumstances and afflictions.

reasonable_visual_inferences: The people of Ammon pause near weapons while Helaman and his brethren address them.
unspecified_visual_details: The setting, clothing, number of people, types of weapons, and words of the persuasion are not specified.

narration.text: they were moved with compassion and were desirous to take up arms in the defence of their country.
they were about to take their weapons of war
they were overpowered by the persuasions of Helaman and his brethren

doctrinal_or_story_notes: The passage reports persuasion but quotes no speech.
Helaman's fear for their souls is stated; it is not a visible event.
prohibited_inventions: Do not invent Helaman's words or depict the oath being broken.
Do not depict the Nephites' afflictions as a simultaneous encounter with the persuasion.

explicit_facts.text: Many sons had not entered the covenant against taking up weapons to defend themselves; those able to bear arms assembled and called themselves Nephites.
They covenanted to fight for Nephite liberty, protect the land even at the cost of their lives, never give up liberty, and defend the Nephites and themselves from bondage.
Two thousand young men entered the covenant and took up weapons to defend their country.
